To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the histone proteins that make up chromatin are passed down from mother to daughter cells during the process of budding yeast cell division and that the histone variants that are inherited are not the same as the variants present in the mother.
1) old histones tend to move from 3′ to 5′ over multiple generations of genomic replication, and 2) maternal histones are inherited over around 400 bp of the genome.

(1) old histones are inherited by daughter cells, (2) old histones move toward the 5′-end of the genome, (3) maternal histones move toward replication origin, (4) maternal histone inheritance is limited to around 400bp, (5) the rate of histone inheritance is not affected by the presence of a centromere, and (6) the rate of inheritance depends on the length of the gene.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the molecular basis of the inheritance of epigenetic states in eukaryotic organisms.
the study of the mechanisms of inheritance of the histone proteins that package the DNA of the chromosomes in eukaryotic cells.
the molecular mechanisms of epigenetic inheritance and the role that epigenetic mechanisms play in the evolution of complex organisms.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

histones are inherited in budding yeast in a non-random, yet stochastic manner, with a preference for old histones to be retained at the 3′ end of genes, and a preference for new histones to be inherited at the 5′ end.
the majority of the histones are not inherited, but that a small fraction of the old histones are inherited in yeast.
histones are inherited in a biased, but not random, manner, and that this inheritance is influenced by both the parental origin of the histone and the position on the chromosome.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we show how the genome is assembled in the context of the nucleus, and how the genome is maintained in the nucleus.
histones move along the genome in a 3’-to-5’ direction over time, and this movement is not random.
the patterns and mechanisms of histone inheritance are highly dynamic, with different mechanisms operating in different regions of the genome and at different times during the cell cycle.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the histone inheritance patterns in yeast are more complicated than previously thought, and the mechanisms that underlie these patterns are likely to be more complex than previously thought.
the histones that were in the genome before replication tend to be replaced with newly synthesized histones.
the inheritance of histone variants is not random, and that the inheritance of specific histones can be predicted based on their position in a gene.
